html:
The Tito Stalin split came on 28 June 1948, when the Soviet led Cominform expelled Yugoslavia, openly breaking the unity of the communist world for the first time.

Tito's Partisans had won power largely on their own, and Tito ran his own foreign policy in the Balkans. Stalin tried to bring him to heel and failed. Yugoslavia purged pro Soviet communists, sending thousands to the prison island of Goli Otok, and took aid from the West. It then built its own model: workers' self management, open borders that let Yugoslavs work abroad, and the Non-Aligned Movement. The split showed that a communist state could defy Moscow and survive.
sum: The Tito Stalin split came on 28 June 1948, when the Soviet led Cominform expelled Yugoslavia, openly breaking the unity of the communist world for the first time.
